Documentation

Everything you need to wire an agent through AgentRaaS: authentication, the two calling styles, MCP, SDKs, and self-hosting reference.

AgentRaaS is the reliability layer between your agents and the APIs they call (Stripe, Twilio, your own internal endpoint, any MCP server). Every call goes through four checks before anything real happens:

  • Run once. The call claims an atomic dedup slot in Redis, so a retry from your agent, your framework or a flaky network gets the first result back instead of a second charge, message or side effect.
  • Allowed? Action policies decide what each agent may do and where it may send data; spend caps limit how often it may do it.
  • Needs a human? Risky calls wait for approval instead of running.
  • Recorded. Every decision lands in one audit log with a per-agent identity, and goes out to your own tools through Prometheus and OpenTelemetry.

New to AgentRaaS? Start with Getting started for the click-by-click walkthrough of connecting your first agent. This page is the reference once you're wiring things up for real.

Quickstart

  1. Register and log in at the dashboard (Cloud), or self-host with ./install.sh. See Self-hosting below.
  2. Click + Connect agent. You get an API key, a webhook URL, and an MCP URL, shown once. Save the API key; it can't be retrieved again.
  3. Add credentials for whatever service you're calling (Credentials panel); AgentRaaS forwards using those, so your agent code never touches a raw upstream API key.
  4. Call AgentRaaS instead of the real API, using either calling style below.

Library mode Free

Exactly-once execution with no AgentRaaS server at all. Decorate any function that has a side effect; retries and concurrent duplicates get the first result back instead of running it again. State lives in a local SQLite file by default, or in your own Redis.

pip install agentraas
from agentraas.local import exactly_once, RedisStore

@exactly_once()                      # SQLite file, one machine
def charge(customer, amount, idempotency_key=None):
    return stripe.Charge.create(customer=customer, amount=amount,
                                idempotency_key=idempotency_key).id

charge("cus_1", 4200)   # runs for real
charge("cus_1", 4200)   # returns the cached id, no second charge

@exactly_once(store=RedisStore("redis://localhost:6379/0"),   # across machines
              key=lambda order: order["id"], ttl=3600)
async def ship(order):
    ...
OptionDefaultWhat it does
storeSQLite fileSQLiteStore(path) for one machine, RedisStore(url) for several (needs pip install redis).
keyall argumentsFunction returning what counts as "the same call", e.g. an order ID.
ttl86400Seconds a completed result is remembered.
wait30Seconds a duplicate waits for an in-flight first call before raising InFlightError.

If the function raises, nothing is cached and a retry runs it again. That includes the case where the provider did the work but the response was lost. Give the function an idempotency_key parameter and pass it to the provider: the decorator fills it with the same value on every retry, so the provider dedupes that case itself. Results must be JSON-serializable.

LangChain & LangGraph Free

Exactly-once tool calls for LangChain agents, create_react_agent and ToolNode. Wrap the tools that have side effects; when the model calls one again with the same arguments, or the graph re-runs the tool node after a crash or retry, the first result comes back instead of a second charge.

pip install "agentraas[langchain]"
from agentraas.langchain import protect_tool

tools = [protect_tool(charge_card), protect_tool(send_email), search]
agent = create_react_agent(model, tools)

Takes the same store, key and ttl options as library mode, e.g. protect_tool(refund, store=RedisStore(url), key=lambda order_id, **_: order_id). Tool results must be JSON-serializable.

CrewAI Free

Exactly-once tool calls for CrewAI agents. Wrap the tools that have side effects, either BaseTool subclasses or @tool functions; when the agent calls one again with the same arguments, or a crew is kicked off again after a crash, the first result comes back instead of a second charge.

pip install "agentraas[crewai]"
from agentraas.crewai import protect_tool

agent = Agent(role="Billing", goal="...", backstory="...",
              tools=[protect_tool(ChargeCardTool()), protect_tool(send_email)])

Same store, key and ttl options as library mode. CrewAI needs Python 3.10 or newer. The original tool object is left unchanged.

Vercel AI SDK Free

Exactly-once tool calls for generateText and streamText. Wrap your tools object; when the model calls a tool again with the same input, or a request is retried, the first result comes back instead of a second charge.

npm install agentraas
import { protectTools, RedisStore } from "agentraas";

const tools = protectTools({ charge, sendEmail, search }, { store: new RedisStore(redis) });
const result = await generateText({ model, tools, prompt });

The key is the tool name plus its input; toolCallId and the other per-call options are passed through, never part of the key. Pass key: (toolName, input) => input.orderId to key on one field. Use MemoryStore for a single process, RedisStore when several serve requests. Results must be JSON-serializable.

MCP wrap Free

Exactly-once tool calls and an audit log for any stdio MCP server. Put agentraas wrap -- in front of the server's own command; everything passes through unchanged, except that an identical call to a write tool (same tool, same arguments) inside the dedup window gets the first call's result back instead of running again.

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "github": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["agentraas", "wrap", "--", "npx", "-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"]
    }
  }
}
OptionDefaultWhat it does
--ttl600Seconds an identical write call is deduplicated.
--dedupe TOOLAlways dedupe this tool, even if it looks read-only. Repeatable.
--no-dedupe TOOLNever dedupe this tool. Repeatable.
--db~/.agentraas/mcp-dedup.dbSQLite file for dedup state.
--log~/.agentraas/mcp-audit.jsonlJSON-lines audit log of every tool call; '' disables it.

Read-only tools always run, so lookups stay fresh: the server's readOnlyHint annotation decides, falling back to names like get_*, list_* and search_*. A failed call (JSON-RPC error or isError: true) is not cached, so a retry runs for real. A deduplicated result carries _meta: {"agentraas/deduplicated": true}.

Chaos tester Free

agentraas-chaos sits between your code and an API. The first time each distinct write request (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) arrives, it lets the request execute and then drops the response: the network failure that turns a retry into a double charge. It then lists every action that executed more than once.

# safe: a built-in mock answers every call
agentraas-chaos --mock -- python my_agent.py

# a real API: use test-mode keys
agentraas-chaos --upstream https://api.stripe.com -- pytest

Your command gets AGENTRAAS_CHAOS_URL (for example http://127.0.0.1:8787) to use as its API base URL. Without a command it runs until Ctrl-C, so you can point an n8n workflow or any other tool at it by hand. It exits with code 1 when it finds a duplicate. A retry that repeats an Idempotency-Key it has already seen counts as protected.

FlagWhat it does
--mockAnswer every call with a fake 200. Nothing real is called.
--upstream URLForward to a real API base URL.
--faultlost-response (default) drops the connection; error-after-commit returns a 502 instead; none only records.
--portLocal port, default 8787.

GitHub Actions

- uses: actions/setup-python@v5
  with: { python-version: "3.12" }
- uses: sumedhchatse/agentraas/src/chaos-action@main
  with:
    run: python my_agent.py      # optional: upstream, fault

Local tunnel

Test webhooks against code running on your laptop without deploying it or configuring a public URL. agentraas tunnel opens a connection to AgentRaaS, prints a public URL, and replays every request sent to that URL against a local port. Available on every plan, including Community.

pip install "agentraas[tunnel]"
agentraas tunnel --port 3000 --org org_acme --agent agent_1 --key ar_live_...

  Tunnel is live: https://agentraas.io/t/tn_3f9c2a71d04b8e65
  Forwarding to:  http://localhost:3000

POST /webhooks/stripe -> 200 (4ms)

Paste the public URL (plus any path, for example /webhooks/stripe) into the provider's webhook settings. The key is the agent API key from the dashboard.

LimitValue
Tunnels per org1 (opening a second closes the first)
Session length2 hours, then re-run the command
Local response timeout30 seconds
Requests through the public URL120/min

Authentication

Every route accepts your API key in a different place depending on the calling style you use; there's no single global header. Keys start with ar_live_ and are shown exactly once when you connect an agent; AgentRaaS only ever stores a hash of it.

Calling styleWhere the key goes
WebhookAuthorization: Bearer <key>
SDK-style RESTx-agentraas-key: <key> header
MCPx-agentraas-key: <key> header

Lost a key? Connect a new agent and revoke the old one from the Credentials panel; there's no way to have a lost key re-displayed.

REST: webhook style

The simplest integration: point any no-code tool (n8n, Make, Zapier) or a plain curl/HTTP client at one URL per agent. org_id and agent_id live in the path, so nothing else needs configuring per request.

POST /v1/webhook/:org_id/:agent_id
curl -X POST https://your-instance/v1/webhook/acme-corp/billing-bot \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ar_live_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "service": "stripe",
    "action": "charge.create",
    "payload": { "amount": 5000, "currency": "usd", "customer": "cus_123" }
  }'
FieldRequiredDescription
serviceYesWhich connector. See Supported services, or a Custom Action's name.
actionYesWhich operation on that service.
payloadNoFields the action needs, matching the real API's own shape.
end_user_idNoYour own identifier for who this action was on behalf of. Shows up in the audit trail.
resource_idNoYour own identifier for what was acted on (an order id, a ticket id, etc.). While one call naming it is in flight, a second call naming the same resource_id gets 409 instead of racing it; the lock is released when the first call finishes.

A successful response, first call vs. a retry of the same request:

→ 200 OK   // first call, forwarded, result cached
{"result":{"status":"success","charge_id":"ch_1N..."}}

→ 200 OK   // identical retry, dedup slot already claimed
{"result":{"status":"success","charge_id":"ch_1N...","deduplicated":true}}

REST: SDK style

Used by the official SDKs (see SDKs): org_id/agent_id travel as headers instead of the URL, so one client instance can be reused across calls without rebuilding a path each time.

POST /v1/sdk/:service/:action
curl -X POST https://your-instance/v1/sdk/stripe/charge.create \
  -H "x-agentraas-key: ar_live_..." \
  -H "x-agentraas-org: acme-corp" \
  -H "x-agentraas-agent: billing-bot" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "amount": 5000, "currency": "usd", "customer": "cus_123" }'

The request body here is the payload directly (no wrapping service/action/payload envelope; those are already in the path and headers). Response shape is identical to the webhook style above.

GET /v1/sdk/whoami

Checks an agent key without doing anything: 200 {"ok": true, "org_id": "..."} for a valid key, 401 for a missing, unknown or revoked one. Useful as a credential test in integrations (the n8n node uses it).

MCP

For Claude Desktop, Cursor, or any MCP client: every tool call through this gateway gets the same dedup, validation, rate-limiting, and audit logging as the REST routes.

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "agentraas": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://your-instance/mcp"]
    }
  }
}
POST /mcp

Standard JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP (tools/list, tools/call). Authenticate with the same x-agentraas-key header as SDK-style REST.

Idempotency & tracing

Optional headers accepted by both the webhook and SDK-style routes, useful once you're running agents in production and want to correlate calls with your own systems:

HeaderPurpose
x-agentraas-idempotency-keyYour own dedup key, if you want to control the dedup window's scope yourself instead of relying on the request body being byte-identical.
x-agentraas-run-idCorrelates every call from one agent "run" together in the audit trail.
x-agentraas-step-idIdentifies which step within a run this call was, for multi-step agent workflows.
x-agentraas-end-userSDK-style equivalent of the webhook body's end_user_id.
x-agentraas-resource-idSDK-style equivalent of the webhook body's resource_id.

What reaches the provider

Every forwarded call carries Idempotency-Key: agentraas-<hash>, one stable value per logical action. It stays the same when AgentRaaS retries, when your agent retries, and when you replay the call from the dead-letter queue, so a provider that honors the header (Stripe and others) runs the action once even if a copy reaches it twice. A Custom Action that sets its own Idempotency-Key header keeps it.

When the provider doesn't answer

If a call times out, or the connection drops after the request was sent, nobody can tell whether it ran. AgentRaaS does not retry it and does not free its dedup slot. You get a 504 with "outcome": "unknown", the call goes to the dead-letter queue, and identical calls get a 409 instead of running again. Replay it from the dead-letter queue to resolve it: the replay reuses the same Idempotency-Key, and once it succeeds, identical calls get its result. A refused connection or DNS failure means nothing was sent, so those are still retried as normal.

Errors

Every error response is a flat JSON object with the same shape, regardless of route:

{ "error": "A human-readable message." }

Some errors add a machine-readable code field alongside error for cases worth branching on in your own code (e.g. EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED), and a few add extra context fields (e.g. replayed: true on a deduplicated dead-letter replay). Check the specific status code first, code isn't present on every error.

StatusMeaning
401Missing or invalid API key.
402Monthly usage limit reached (Cloud only; self-hosted has no enforced limit on any tier).
403Authenticated, but not permitted for this org/action, or blocked by an action policy (the message names it).
422Request validation failed. Check the message for which field.
429Rate limit exceeded. See Plans & limits.
409An identical call is still in flight, or an earlier identical call has an unknown outcome (see Idempotency & tracing).
502/503The upstream service (Stripe, Twilio, etc.) was unreachable or errored; AgentRaaS fails closed rather than silently succeeding un-deduplicated.
504The upstream didn't respond, so the action may or may not have run. Not retried; "outcome": "unknown" in the body.

SDKs

Thin, dependency-light wrappers over the SDK-style REST routes above. Both work against Cloud or any self-hosted instance.

Python

pip install agentraas
import agentraas

client = agentraas.Client(
    agentraas_key="ar_live_...",
    org_id="acme-corp",
    agent_id="billing-bot",
    base_url="https://your-instance",
)

result = client.call("stripe", "charge.create", {"amount": 5000, "currency": "usd"})

TypeScript / JavaScript

Install from npm: npm install agentraas. Pass { idempotencyKey } as a fourth argument to call() to choose your own dedup key.

import { Client } from "agentraas";

const client = new Client({
  agentraasKey: "ar_live_...",
  orgId: "acme-corp",
  agentId: "billing-bot",
  baseUrl: "https://your-instance",
});

const result = await client.call("stripe", "charge.create", { amount: 5000, currency: "usd" });

Both SDKs are MIT-licensed. Neither retries automatically: since AgentRaaS claims the dedup slot server-side before forwarding, your own retry logic (as aggressive as you want) is always safe to call again with the same payload.

Supported services

Curated, pre-configured integrations, no code required:

Stripe, Twilio, HubSpot, Calendly, Shopify, Zoho, Razorpay, WhatsApp, Zapier, Make, Adyen, Mollie, Airwallex, Xendit, PayPal, Salesforce, Slack, Klarna, Paystack, GoCardless, Opn Payments, plus the built-in mockpay for safe testing.

Need something not on this list? See Custom Actions below.

Custom Actions

Register any endpoint yourself from the Custom actions panel (any URL, any auth type) and it gets the same dedup, audit trail, and SSRF guarding (so it can't be pointed at your own internal infrastructure) as a curated service. Call it exactly like a built-in service, using its registered name as service.

Undo log Free

When an agent does something it shouldn't have, undo it from the dashboard (Monitor → Undo actions). Every action that ran and has a known reverse is recorded for 30 days with what reversing it takes: a Stripe charge is refunded, a Slack message is deleted. Each entry can be undone once: two clicks at the same moment still run the reverse once, and it is sent with the Idempotency-Key agentraas-undo-<id>. If the provider doesn't answer, the entry is marked outcome unknown and not retried. Actions without a reverse (an SMS, an email) don't appear. Duplicates AgentRaaS caught and failed calls never ran, so there is nothing to undo.

Built in: stripe charge.create → charge.refund, slack message.post → message.delete, and mockpay payment.create → payment.refund for trying it. For your own endpoint, register its reverse as another custom action and name it when you register the action:

POST /api/v1/custom-actions
{ "org_id": "org_acme", "name": "create_ticket", "target_url": "https://api.example.com/tickets",
  "undo": { "action": "close_ticket",
            "with": { "ticket_id": "response.id", "reason": "payload.title" } } }

with fills each field of the reverse call from the original's response (response.<path>) or payload (payload.<path>); dotted paths, array items by index. If a value is missing the action is not recorded as undoable. API: GET /api/v1/undo-log?org_id= lists entries, POST /api/v1/undo-log/<id>/undo undoes one (any member who can write to the org). Undo calls appear in the audit log with status undo and are never billed.

Record and replay Free

Test an agent against what real providers answered, without calling them again. Run it once with X-AgentRaaS-Record: <name> on its calls (webhook or SDK endpoint): every call that succeeds is kept under that name for 30 days, payload and response encrypted. Then run it again, in a test or in CI or after changing a prompt, with X-AgentRaaS-Replay: <name>: each call is answered from the recording and nothing reaches the provider, nothing is deduplicated and nothing counts as usage.

curl -X POST https://agentraas.io/v1/webhook/org_acme/support-bot \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENT_KEY" -H "X-AgentRaaS-Replay: refund-flow" \
  -H "X-AgentRaaS-Run-Id: ci-1234" \
  -d '{"service":"stripe","action":"charge.create","payload":{"amount":500}}'

{ "upstream_response": { ... as recorded ... }, "reqId": "...",
  "replay": { "recording": "refund-flow", "position": 1, "payload_matches": true } }

Answers are played back in order: the second stripe charge.create of a replay gets the second one recorded. payload_matches is false when the agent now sends something different, and a call the recording doesn't have gets a 404, so a test can fail on either. The position is kept per agent and X-AgentRaaS-Run-Id for an hour: send a new run id to start from the top. From the SDKs: Client(..., record="refund-flow") or replay="refund-flow", run_id=... in Python (0.10.0), record / replay / runId in the JS Client options (0.4.0). Only successful, non-streaming calls are recorded. MCP calls record and replay the same way: set the headers on the MCP connection (X-AgentRaaS-Run-Id, or a run_id tool argument). API: GET /api/v1/recordings?org_id= lists recordings, GET /api/v1/recordings/<name>?org_id= shows each call with its payload and response, DELETE on the same URL removes it.

Action policies Free

Decide what each agent is allowed to do: the support agent may refund up to 50, may never delete a customer, may only email your customers' domains. Set them in the dashboard (Rules, Action policies) or through the API. Every matching policy applies, and a refused call gets a 403 naming the policy and is recorded in the audit log.

POST /api/v1/action-policies
{ "org_id": "org_acme", "agent_id": "support-bot",
  "service": "stripe", "action": "refunds.create", "effect": "require",
  "fields": { "amount": { "max": 5000 } } }

{ "org_id": "org_acme", "agent_id": "support-bot",
  "service": "hubspot", "action": "*", "effect": "deny" }

{ "org_id": "org_acme", "service": "resend", "action": "emails.send",
  "effect": "require", "fields": { "to": { "domains": ["acme.com"] } } }

{ "org_id": "org_acme", "service": "resend", "action": "*", "effect": "require",
  "fields": { "*": { "no_secrets": true }, "to": { "new_destination": true } },
  "on_violation": "hitl" }
FieldWhat it does
agent_idOptional. Leave it out to apply to every agent in the org.
actionA service action, or * for every action of the service.
effectdeny never allows the call; require allows it only when the payload passes fields.
fieldsSame syntax as validation rules (min, max, enum, format, required, ...), plus domains: an email or URL field (or a list of them) must be on one of these domains or a subdomain. Two rules guard against a prompt-injected agent: no_secrets: true refuses a call whose field contains an API key, token or private key (use the field name * to scan the whole payload), and new_destination: true sends a call to an email address, phone number or URL host this org has never approved for approval once; approving it remembers the destination (needs on_violation: hitl).
on_violationblock (default), or hitl to send the call for approval instead. A block always wins over an approval.

Rules as code Free

Keep an org's dedup rules, validation rules, action policies and spend caps in a YAML file in your repo, review changes like code, and apply them from CI. agentraas apply makes the server match the file through the normal API: it creates what is missing and replaces what changed. Running it twice changes nothing.

pip install "agentraas[apply]"
# agentraas.yaml
apiVersion: agentraas.io/v1alpha1
kind: DedupRule
metadata:
  name: charge-once        # for people reading the file; not stored
  org: org_acme
spec:
  service: stripe
  action: charges.create
  fields: [customer, amount]
  ttlSeconds: 300
---
apiVersion: agentraas.io/v1alpha1
kind: ActionPolicy
metadata: {org: org_acme}
spec: {agentId: support-bot, service: stripe, action: refunds.create, effect: require, fields: {amount: {max: 5000}}}
---
apiVersion: agentraas.io/v1alpha1
kind: SpendCap
metadata: {org: org_acme}
spec: {service: stripe, action: refunds.create, window: day, maxCalls: 100, onExceed: block}
export AGENTRAAS_URL=https://agentraas.example.com
export AGENTRAAS_EMAIL=ci@acme.com AGENTRAAS_PASSWORD=...   # a user with write access to the org
agentraas apply -f agentraas.yaml --dry-run   # print the plan, change nothing
agentraas apply -f agentraas.yaml             # apply it
agentraas apply -f agentraas.yaml --prune     # also delete rules the file doesn't list
KindSame asOne rule per
DedupRuleDedup rulesservice + action
ValidationRuleValidation rulesservice + action
ActionPolicyAction policiesagent + service + action + effect
SpendCapSpend capsagent + service + action + window

Spec keys are the API's fields in camelCase (ttl_seconds becomes ttlSeconds, on_violation becomes onViolation). Without --prune, rules made in the dashboard are left alone; with it, every rule of these four kinds in the orgs the file names that the file doesn't list is deleted. The command exits non-zero if any change fails, so a CI job fails with it.

Inbound webhooks Enterprise

For the reverse direction: a third party (e.g. WhatsApp) calling into your system. AgentRaaS verifies the provider's real signature (HMAC or ECDSA, whichever that provider uses) before forwarding the payload on to your own destination URL, so you get signature verification without implementing it per provider.

GET / POST /v1/inbound/:token

Manage receivers from the dashboard's Outage alerts panel, or via /api/v1/inbound-webhooks.

Self-hosting

Self-hosted AgentRaaS has no enforced monthly usage limit on any tier; it's your infrastructure. One Docker Compose service, no data leaving your control.

./install.sh

This generates fresh secrets, runs migrations, and starts the stack. Key environment variables (full reference in .env.example):

VariablePurpose
JWT_SECRETSigns dashboard sessions. Required; the server won't start without it.
CREDENTIALS_ENCRYPTION_KEYEncrypts stored service credentials at rest. Required, 32 bytes.
PUBLIC_URLUsed for email links and the Connect Agent webhook/MCP URLs. Set this to your real domain.
AGENT_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINPer-key rate limit across webhook/SDK/MCP routes. Default 300.
CLIENT_IP_HEADERBehind a reverse proxy, the header it sets with the real client IP (x-real-ip for nginx, cf-connecting-ip behind Cloudflare), so login and signup rate limits apply per visitor. Only name a header your proxy always sets; unset uses the connecting address. Never x-forwarded-for: clients can prepend to it.
PROXY_TIMEOUT_SECONDSHow long one forwarded call may take (default 30). A call that hits it is held as outcome unknown, not retried.
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINTOptional. Sends every call AgentRaaS handles (ran, deduplicated, blocked, held for approval) as an OpenTelemetry span over OTLP/HTTP to your collector or tracing tool (Langfuse, Grafana, Datadog, Honeycomb, Jaeger), named execute_tool service.action per the GenAI conventions. Calls sharing an X-AgentRaaS-Run-Id share a trace. Auth goes in OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS (key=value,key2=value2); OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT takes a full URL instead. Payloads are never exported.
SMTP_*Optional. Without it, password-reset links are logged server-side instead of emailed.

Self-hosting includes every feature (approvals, SSO, DLP, agent identity) with no license token: compose.yaml builds the full edition and sets ENTERPRISE_MODE=true.

Kubernetes (Helm)

The repo ships a Helm chart in infra/helm/agentraas. It runs the Community image (ghcr.io/sumedhchatse/agentraas, tag = the chart's app version) with a bundled single-instance Postgres and Redis, or with your own.

git clone https://github.com/sumedhchatse/agentraas && cd agentraas
helm install agentraas ./infra/helm/agentraas \
  --set publicUrl=https://agentraas.example.com \
  --set ingress.enabled=true --set ingress.host=agentraas.example.com \
  --set clientIpHeader=x-real-ip

With a managed database and Redis:

helm install agentraas ./infra/helm/agentraas \
  --set postgresql.enabled=false --set externalDatabase.url=postgres://user:pass@host:5432/agentraas \
  --set redis.enabled=false --set externalRedis.url=redis://host:6379
ValueWhat it does
publicUrlThe URL people reach the dashboard at (email links, Connect Agent URLs).
existingSecretA Secret holding JWT_SECRET, CREDENTIALS_ENCRYPTION_KEY and, with an external database, DATABASE_URL. Leave empty and the chart generates them on first install and keeps them on upgrade.
clientIpHeaderThe header your ingress writes with the client IP (see CLIENT_IP_HEADER in Self-hosting).
metricsTokenTurns on /metrics.
extraEnvAny other environment variable, e.g. SMTP_HOST, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT.
replicaCountKeep 1 with the bundled datastores. The API itself is stateless (dedup state lives in Redis).

Every database migration runs before the API starts, in an init container that holds a Postgres advisory lock so replicas don't race; all migrations are safe to re-run. The API runs with a read-only root filesystem and is probed on /health.

Back up CREDENTIALS_ENCRYPTION_KEY (in the generated Secret). Without it, the third-party credentials AgentRaaS stores can't be decrypted. Redis holds the dedup slots: run it with persistence, or a restart reopens recent calls to duplicates.

Metrics (Prometheus)

GET /metrics serves Prometheus text format: how many calls AgentRaaS handled and how long it took to answer them, by service and outcome. It is off (404) until you set METRICS_TOKEN, and then needs that token as a bearer token. There is no org label, so one token never reveals another tenant's traffic.

# prometheus.yml
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: agentraas
    scheme: https
    authorization:
      credentials: your-metrics-token
    static_configs:
      - targets: [agentraas.example.com]
MetricTypeLabels
agentraas_calls_totalcounterservice, status (success, deduplicated, blocked, error, ...)
agentraas_call_duration_mshistogram (5 ms to 10 s)service, status
# duplicates caught per second, by service
sum by (service) (rate(agentraas_calls_total{status="deduplicated"}[5m]))
# p95 time to answer
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(agentraas_call_duration_ms_bucket[5m])))

Counters live in memory and reset when the server restarts, which Prometheus' rate() handles. For per-call detail (which agent, which run), use the OpenTelemetry export instead.

Latency

Every call passes through auth, the dedup claim, spend caps and the audit write before it is forwarded. Measured on one machine (Intel Core i3-12100, 8 GB RAM, local stack, 500 sequential calls per row, three runs):

p50p95
Added by AgentRaaS to a forwarded call2.1 to 2.4 ms2.9 to 3.7 ms
Retried duplicate (answered from cache, upstream never called)2.1 to 2.3 ms total3.0 to 3.5 ms total

Network distance between your agent and AgentRaaS comes on top of this. Self-hosting next to your agent keeps that near zero. Reproduce it with python3 infra/scripts/bench-overhead.py against your own instance.

Troubleshooting

Ordered from quick checks to deeper digging: work down a list until the problem is gone. The free tools (library mode, MCP wrap, chaos tester) run entirely on your machine, so an AgentRaaS Cloud outage never affects them.

Start here: 60-second checks

  1. Is the server up? Cloud: /status, or curl https://agentraas.io/health should return {"ok":true,"postgres":true,"redis":true}. Self-hosted: curl http://localhost:13001/health.
  2. Read the response body. Every error has a message and a reqId; the table below says what each status means.
  3. Upgrade the package: pip install -U agentraas. Check what you have with pip show agentraas.

API responses (webhook, SDK-style REST, MCP)

StatusMeaningWhat to do
400Unknown service.action, missing fields, or no Custom Action with that name for this orgCheck spelling against Supported services, or register it as a Custom Action.
401API key missing, wrong, or revoked for this org and agentCheck the header and the org/agent IDs in the URL; connect a new agent if the key was lost.
402Free Cloud account's monthly limit reachedSelf-host for free (no limit on any tier), or wait for the monthly reset.
409An identical request is still being processed, or an earlier identical call timed out with an unknown outcomeStill processing: retry shortly and you get the first call's result. "Outcome is unknown": see A call timed out below; retrying won't run it.
422The payload failed a validation ruleThe message names the field; fix the payload or the org's rule.
429This agent's per-minute rate limitBack off and retry; raise the limit if the volume is legitimate.
502 / 503The upstream API is failing, or its circuit breaker is openCheck the provider's status page. AgentRaaS fails closed on purpose; the breaker tries again by itself after 30 seconds.
504The provider didn't answer in time, so the action may or may not have runNot retried on purpose. See A call timed out below.
500AgentRaaS itself failedRetry with backoff. If it keeps happening, contact us with the reqId.

A call timed out (504 "outcome unknown", then 409)

The provider never answered, so nobody knows whether the action ran. AgentRaaS stops there instead of guessing: it doesn't retry, and identical calls get a 409 until you resolve it. That is what keeps a slow provider from turning into a double charge. Work down this list:

  1. Check the provider. Look in its own dashboard or request log around the time of the call. Every call AgentRaaS sends carries Idempotency-Key: agentraas-..., which you can search for (in Stripe: Developers, Logs).
  2. It ran, and the provider supports Idempotency-Key (Stripe does, for 24 hours): open Failed Requests in the dashboard and click Replay. The provider hands back the original result instead of running it again, and your agent's identical calls start getting that result.
  3. It did not run: click Replay and it runs once.
  4. It ran, but the provider has no Idempotency-Key support (or its window has passed): click Dismiss, not Replay. The 409s are correct and stop when the dedup window ends (24 hours by default).
  5. You're sure it did not run and want your agent's own retry to go through: send the call with a new x-agentraas-idempotency-key. Don't do this if it might have run. 
    curl -X POST https://agentraas.io/v1/webhook/YOUR_ORG/YOUR_AGENT \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ar_live_..." \
  -H "x-agentraas-idempotency-key: order-1042-retry-1" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service":"stripe","action":"charge.create","payload":{"amount":5000,"currency":"usd"}}'
  6. Use Replay, not Edit & Replay, to resolve a timeout: an edited payload is a new request and goes out without the original key.
  7. Happens often with one provider? Self-hosted: raise PROXY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default 30) in .env and restart. Cloud: contact us with a reqId.

Library mode (@exactly_once)

Basic

  • The function ran twice. By default a call's key is all of its arguments, so a timestamp or random ID among them makes every call unique. Pass key= with what really identifies the action (an order ID).
  • It ran once per machine. SQLiteStore is per machine. Use RedisStore when several machines run the same code.
  • TypeError about JSON. Results are stored as JSON: return ids and plain dicts, not SDK objects.

Intermediate

  • It ran again after the provider already did the work. The response was lost, the function raised, and a raising call is never cached. Add an idempotency_key parameter and send it to the provider (see Library mode).
  • InFlightError. A duplicate waited wait seconds for the first call to finish. If the first process was killed mid-call, its slot stays pending until ttl expires.
  • An old result keeps coming back. It's inside the ttl window (default 24 hours). Lower ttl, or clear the state (below).

Advanced

# see what's stored (SQLite)
sqlite3 agentraas-dedup.db "SELECT key, substr(value,1,60), datetime(expires_at,'unixepoch') FROM dedup;"
# clear everything: delete the file (SQLite), or in Redis:
redis-cli --scan --pattern 'dedup:local:*' | xargs -r redis-cli del

MCP wrap

Basic

  • The server doesn't show up, or uvx: command not found. Install uv, or pip install agentraas and use "command": "agentraas" with "args": ["wrap", "--", ...].
  • The server fails to start. Run the server's own command alone in a terminal first. Then run uvx agentraas wrap -- <same command>: it should sit waiting for input, which is normal for a stdio MCP server.

Intermediate

  • A write tool isn't deduplicated. Tools the server marks read-only, or named like get_*, list_*, search_*, always run. Force it with --dedupe TOOL_NAME.
  • A tool is deduplicated when repeats are intentional. Use --no-dedupe TOOL_NAME, or shorten the window with --ttl (seconds, default 600).
  • See what happened. Every tool call is logged: tail ~/.agentraas/mcp-audit.jsonl. The outcome is executed, deduplicated, failed or passthrough.

Advanced

  • Reset all dedup state: delete ~/.agentraas/mcp-dedup.db.
  • Wrapper and server errors go to stderr, which your MCP client captures in its logs (Claude Desktop: Settings, Developer).
  • "Identical call still in flight" means a duplicate arrived while a slow first call was running; it's refused rather than re-run. Raise --wait for tools that take longer than 30 seconds.

Chaos tester

  • Basic: "0 write requests". Your code didn't use AGENTRAAS_CHAOS_URL as its API base URL. "Address already in use": pass --port.
  • Intermediate: a duplicate you think is fine. The same method, path and body really executed twice. If the provider dedupes by key, send an Idempotency-Key header; retries that reuse it count as protected.
  • Intermediate: retries never flagged. If each retry's body differs (a timestamp inside it), they aren't identical requests. That also defeats payload-based dedup, so use a stable key.
  • Advanced. --fault error-after-commit for clients that retry on 5xx rather than dropped connections; --fault none just records. Against real APIs, use test-mode keys.

Self-hosted server

  • Basic. podman ps (or docker ps): are the API, Postgres and Redis containers running? Then curl localhost:13001/health.
  • Intermediate: the API container exits at start. Read its logs. A missing or empty JWT_SECRET, DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL or CREDENTIALS_ENCRYPTION_KEY is the usual cause.
  • Intermediate: relation "..." does not exist. A migration wasn't applied. Run every file in infra/migrations/ in order; they're safe to re-run.
  • Intermediate: approvals, SSO or DLP missing. Check that ENTERPRISE_MODE=true reaches the container and that the image was built with --features enterprise (the default Containerfile does).
  • Intermediate: no verification email. Without SMTP_* settings the link is written to the logs instead.
  • Advanced: rebuilt, but the old behavior remains. Recreate the container (up -d --force-recreate) and check it runs the new image. If the build "succeeded" suspiciously fast, check disk space: a full disk can fail the compile while the wrapper still reports success.
  • Advanced: trace one request. Grep the API logs for the reqId from the response.

Still stuck?

Email hello@agentraas.io or open a GitHub issue with: what you ran, the full response body including the reqId, your agentraas version or server commit, and whether it's Cloud or self-hosted. Never include API keys or credentials.
